thread:
sasha_support: Hey team — escalation from BetaSearch. Their embeddings vectors/sec dropped ~6x around 18:00 UTC yesterday while token generation rates were steady. They report high queueing and some 429s. Billing/auth look normal. Can someone triage?

alex_ml: Do we have a sample request and the embedding length they observed? Model + route?

sasha_support: Pasting their sanitized curl and response snippet:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"rw-embed-large\",\"input\":[\"...\"],\"batch_size\":32}'
```

Response shows \"embedding\": [ ... ] length = 512
They were previously on rw-embed-large-v1 (768) and migrated to rw-embed-large-512-quant last week per billing note.

jerry_infra: Looking at infra metrics for the embeddings fleet at 18:00 UTC: GPU util jumped to ~96% and stayed high; queue_depth (per-shard) spiked from ~12 to 180 for ~25 minutes. Autoscaler logged a downscale event at 17:59 and then an upscale at 18:05 (weird timing). No host OOMs.

priya_sre: Any recent rollout that could alter batching or kernel selection? I see a config change deployed 2026-03-09 17:58 that adjusted batch window logic. Canary targets were set for token routes but a label mismatch might have included embeddings.

alex_ml: Hypothesis: a variant/quantized model got routed to a kernel path that's suboptimal for 512-d vectors, increasing per-request overhead. Also microbatching frequency increased if batch_window_ms got reduced, which raises CPU->GPU transfer overhead.

sasha_support: I ran a repro on staging using customer payload (same input distribution, using rw-embed-large-512-quant). Staging vectors/sec is ~2.8x slower than baseline. Repro command:

```
# stress runner
python tools/stress_embed.py --model rw-embed-large-512-quant --concurrency 40 --batch-size 32 --duration 600
```

Logs show many small batches (<=8 items) and per-batch overhead ~9-12ms.

jerry_infra: Attaching short log excerpt from runtime:

```
[2026-03-09T18:01:03Z] shard=embed-1 batch_size=6 exec_ms=11 copy_in_ms=4 copy_out_ms=3 kernel_path=quantized_int8
[2026-03-09T18:01:03Z] shard=embed-1 batch_size=2 exec_ms=9 copy_in_ms=4 kernel_path=quantized_int8
[2026-03-09T18:01:04Z] shard=embed-1 batch_size=16 exec_ms=45 copy_in_ms=6 kernel_path=fused_fp16
```

Note: interleaved small micro-batches are saturating GPU with many launches.

priya_sre: I kicked off a canary audit: the batch_window_ms flag was accidentally rolled to 4ms for the embeddings route in the canary group (intended only for token gen routes). That explains the microbatching. Rolling back the flag to 12ms for embeddings now.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated for config 'batch_window_ms' on route 'embeddings' -> from 4ms to 12ms. Rollback started by priya_sre.

alex_ml: Also toggled model-variant routing to prefer fused_fp16 kernel for rw-embed-large-512-quant while we investigate the quantized kernel path. This should reduce kernel launch count.

jerry_infra: After rollback (18:12 UTC) metrics show queue depth falling back to normal (~10) and GPU utilization steady ~70%. Staging vectors/sec returned to baseline within ~90s.

beta_search_bot: Confirmed from customer: vectors/sec back to expected levels, no more 429s. Thanks for the quick help! :tada:

sasha_support: Great. Root cause: bad canary config that reduced embeddings batch window, causing excessive micro-batches and kernel-launch overhead on quantized variant; compounded by a transient downscale during the spike.

priya_sre: Action items: 1) revert canary target rules so embedding routes are excluded from token-specific batch-window rollouts; 2) add guard in deploy pipeline to prevent batch_window_ms < 8ms for embeddings; 3) add an alert for sudden queue_depth > 50 for more than 60s.

sasha_support: Marking this P1 until alerts+guard are in place. I'll follow up with the customer thread. :eyes:
